surprises.description: Piedmont’s leasing economics were much stronger than the preview’s expected cash-spread range: cash and accrual spreads reached 26% and 35%, respectively, and net effective rent after CapEx rose to a new high of $29.31 per square foot. The preview cited 8%–14% as the expected cash-spread range and the prior quarter’s $25.56 as the record net effective rent.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash and accrual leasing spreads reached 26% and 35% respectively”; net effective rents after CapEx “hit an all-time high of $29.31 per square foot.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “cash spreads 8–14%”; it also cited Q2’s “record net effective rent of $25.56/sf.”

surprises.description: The signed-but-not-commenced pipeline was materially smaller than the preview’s stated baseline, reducing the near-term occupancy and revenue conversion expected from leases already signed.
surprises.fact_evidence: The pipeline represents “roughly $29 million of annual revenue, or 410 basis points of occupancy.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the backlog was “$39M of annualized cash rent = ~570bp of future occupancy.”

surprises.description: Same-store NOI and its outlook were stronger than the preview’s expectation of cash growth decelerating and accrual growth reaching only mid-single digits. Q3 accrual growth was 7%, and full-year cash guidance now reaches 8.5%, above the preview’s 8% upper end.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q3 same-store NOI grew “approximately 8% on a cash basis and 7% on an accrual basis,” with full-year guidance of “7.5%-8.5% cash and 5%-6% accrual.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said full-year guidance was “5–8% on both bases,” expected “2H cash deceleration,” and called for accrual growth “accelerating toward mid-single digits.”

surprises.description: Full-year core FFO guidance was raised to $1.55–$1.57, modestly above the preview’s central expectation of $1.53–$1.55 and one cent above its broader expected range at the high end. The preview did expect a raise to reflect the refinancing, so the upside was limited rather than wholly unexpected.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “raised and narrowed” 2026 core FFO guidance to “$1.55-$1.57,” now “$0.06 above original guidance at the midpoint.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was “Narrowed to upper half, $1.53–$1.55”; it said a raise to “$1.53–$1.56” would bank the refinancing benefit.

surprises.description: The refinancing lowered the weighted average cost of debt further than the preview anticipated: the preview expected a step-down toward 5.0%–5.1%, while management reported 4.8%. The transaction itself was already known before the release.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company issued “$230 million of 2.875% exchangeable notes” to redeem the remaining 9.250% notes, “cutting weighted average cost of debt over 70 bps to 4.8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said weighted average cost of debt “should step down from 5.50% toward ~5.0–5.1%.”

surprises.description: Piedmont disclosed an acquisition in Arlington at better initial economics than the preview’s general acquisition outlook: the property was 83% leased with a 10% going-in cap rate and potential returns of 12%, versus the preview’s expectation of 70%–80% leased acquisitions at high-single-digit initial yields. The preview did anticipate a Northern Virginia acquisition pipeline, but not this specific purchase.
surprises.fact_evidence: Piedmont acquired “the 83% leased 4075 Wilson Boulevard in Arlington for ~$52 million ($280/sf) at an estimated going-in 10% cap rate with potential to drive returns to 12%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the acquisition pipeline as “Dallas / Northern Virginia, 70–80% leased, high-single-digit going-in yields stabilizing to low double digits.”

surprises.description: Piedmont contracted to sell Enclave Place in Houston and earmark most of the proceeds for debt repayment, a specific asset sale and use of proceeds not anticipated in the preview. This supports the preview’s deleveraging objective, though the call facts do not provide a realized leverage ratio.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company contracted to sell Enclave Place for “$81.75 million (closing Q4 2026),” with “~$80 million of proceeds earmarked to pay down the $152 million line balance.”

surprises.description: Management described deliberately holding larger vacant blocks, including about 350,000 square feet in Atlanta despite roughly 400,000 square feet of prospects. That can defer occupancy conversion versus the preview’s focus on converting the signed pipeline, although management cited a 10%–15% embedded mark-to-market as upside; it also identified D.C. and Ballston as weak-growth submarkets.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management is “deliberately holding larger blocks,” including “~350,000 sf of Central Perimeter Atlanta vacancy with ~400,000 sf of prospects,” estimates a “10%-15% embedded mark-to-market,” and cited D.C. and Ballston as “the weakest-growth submarkets.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted the “leased-vs-economic occupancy gap,” said to “watch SNC dollars and commencement timing,” and noted management’s goal of occupancy in the “low 90s by 2027.”
